Step 3: The triangle inequality states that the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side. Applying this to the given triangle, we get:
- 200 + 240 > 300 (satisfied)
- 200 + 300 > 240 (satisfied)
- 240 + 300 > 200 (satisfied)

Step 4: Since the triangle is convex, the side lengths must also satisfy the condition that the longest side is less than the sum of the other two sides. In this case, the longest side is 300, so we have:
- 300 < 200 + 240 (satisfied)

- 200/x = 240/(x+y)

where y and z are the additional segments on the sides of the hexagon.
